title: Health
description: How the pipeline itself is doing: what the last run did, which sources are degraded, which quality gates passed, and how a handful of run-level measurements have moved. Assembled from the run manifest, the gate report and the bronze snapshot times — never measured here, so the page cannot hold a second opinion about health that disagrees with the manifest (DL-41).

contract_version.description: Additive at v1: a client that has never heard of this artefact keeps working.

generated_at.description: UTC (DL-11). Every age on this page is measured from here, not from the reader's clock, so a stale cached copy reports the ages it was published with rather than ages that keep growing.

sources.description: One entry per data source the run knew about. Source names are DATA, discovered from the registry and the bronze store — no consumer of this artefact may branch on one (Invariant 1, DP-01).

gates.description: The gate report from this run, or null when none was published with it. Nullable rather than defaulted to a pass: a gate report that is missing has proved nothing, and rendering that as 'all clear' is exactly the silent wrongness the gates exist to catch (DP-13, DP-15).

metrics_history.description: Recent runs as a short series, or null when no history could be assembled. Nullable on purpose: the page degrades to 'no history yet' rather than to an error (DP-15).

health_run.description: The manifest excerpt: what the last run was, and how it ended.

run_id.description: The same id meta.json carries. Traces back to the full manifest on disk (DP-11).

git_dirty.description: True when the working tree had uncommitted changes. Such a run is not reproducible from its recorded inputs, and the page says so rather than leaving it implied.

finished_at.description: Null when the run did not reach the end. A manifest is written after every stage, so an unfinished run still publishes what it got through.

status.description: The run's own outcome. Null while it is still in flight — which is the state of the run that wrote this file.

stages.description: Every stage the run recorded, in the order it ran them.

error.description: Why the stage failed, when it did. Present so a failure can be read here rather than only in a CI log that expires.

health_source.description: One source's freshness and status. `source` is an opaque label from the data: render it, never test it.

status.description: `degraded` means the run continued without this source's fields (NFR-15, DP-15). `unknown` means the source has data on disk but this run recorded nothing about it — which is not the same as healthy, and is not shown as healthy.

detail.description: The derivation behind `degraded`: the exception class the stage caught, or the reason it recorded. A flag without its reason is an assertion (DP-09).

degraded_at_stage.description: Which stage recorded the degradation. Fetching and conforming fail differently and are worth telling apart.

observed_at.description: When this source's freshest snapshot was captured. Null when it has never been captured.

age_seconds.description: `generated_at` minus `observed_at`. Published rather than left to the browser so the number cannot drift with the reader's clock or with how long a cached page has been open.

resources.description: Resource name to row or record count, exactly as the run recorded it.

cache_hits.description: A run served entirely from cache is a legitimate, fast run — and also the reason a source can be 'ok' while its data is older than the run. Published so the two are distinguishable.

health_gates.description: The quality gate report. A blocking failure means nothing was published and the last good artefact is still live (Invariant 7) — so a health page showing a blocked run is being served by the run before it.

passed.description: False only when an error-severity gate failed. A failed warning still publishes.

skipped.description: A gate whose table was absent. Distinct from passing: a gate that never ran proves nothing.

class.description: Which kind of assertion this is — shape, range, referential integrity, or freshness and volume.

message.description: Why it landed where it did, in words, whether it passed or failed. This is the reason a failure can be acted on without opening a log.

requirement.description: The requirement this gate protects (DP-14). A gate nobody can trace to a requirement is one that gets deleted by whoever it inconveniences.

health_metrics_history.description: A short rolling series over recent runs. Oldest first.

derived_from.description: Where the series came from. The shape here is the contract; the storage behind it is not, so this value may change without a schema change (DL-41).

health_metrics_point.description: One run's measurements. Every field but the id is nullable, because a run that failed early recorded fewer of them, and a gap must draw as a gap rather than as a zero.

solve_seconds.description: How long the squad MILP took. The measurement that says whether the optimiser is still comfortably inside the pre-deadline window.

rows_total.description: Total conformed silver rows. The volume signal: a source returning 30 players instead of 700 produces a perfectly valid, perfectly wrong silver layer, and this is where that shows.

rows.description: Per-table row counts for the same run.

r_squared_on_price.description: R-15's PRICE-DEPENDENCE DIAGNOSTIC, not a measure of accuracy: how much of the forecast is explained by price and position alone. High is bad. Skill is measured against a baseline in the backtest and reported in the model card (DP-12), deliberately not here.
